newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch trading firm Internatio-Mueller profit jumps.
newsitem.headline: Dutch trading firm Internatio-Mueller profit jumps.

text.p: Dutch transport and trading group Internatio-Mueller announced a 15 percent jump in 1996 net profits to 98.1 million guilders ($51.7 million), adding that acquisitions and organic growth would fuel future earnings.
"We expect further growth of activities through acquisitions and through organic growth," the company said in a statement.
The results bettered analysts forecasts which ranged between 91 and 98 million guilders. The shares were up 0.50 guilders at 57.70 guilders against the backdrop of a weak Amsterdam bourse.
The company increased its dividend to 1.40 guilders from 1.20 in 1995.
Analysts agreed the company looked in good shape.

"The company looks good, it has a positive and solid cash flow. If you look at the acquisitions made in the second half of 1996, these will add to earnings growth in 1997," said Tom Muller, analyst at NIB Securities.

He predicted an earnings growth of at least 10 percent in 1997, giving earnings per share of 4.45 guilders. Further ahead, the outlook was equally bright, he added and said that over the next five years Internatio-Mueller should generate an average 11 percent annual growth.
"Their technical installation division is picking up. They are now ending loss-making contracts and entering into new more profitable ones with added-value," Muller said. ($ = 1.897 Dutch Guilders)
